review_title: Works Well, but instructions could be better written
review_text: I like this Blurex internet repeater because it works like a champ, but I wish it had been a bit easier to install and the instructions could have been written better. Part of the problem is the print is very tiny, and I'm legally blind. I managed to get the job done without sighted help but not without a lot of magnification. It took me a couple of tries to get the installation to work right but finally I managed and now have a very strong signal throughout the house. What I failed to recognize though is the setup was not only "configuring" the repeater, it was also configuring the computer on which I ran the installation. had I realized what it was going to do I would not have tried it on my brand new desktop computer that was convenient for running the installation at the time, since that computer was going to be hardwired and not depend on wireless. The result is that while I set up the repeater, the process also reworked my computer settings making it only pick up that repeater and the only way I could figure out how to return things on that computer to normal was a system restore. i redid the setup on the laptop that my wife would use out in her office and the setup went a lot better that time. However, I found out that when I took that same laptop on a trip a few days ago, I used a router that the laptop always worked well with and I could direct the computer to that D-Link router for the short trip but I could not get the computer to again work off a wired signal, since the setup to the repeater completely changed the computer's internet hookup. Maybe I'm asking too much but I thought the setup would just change wireless configuration and not mess up any ethernet-connected settings. So one day soon I'll have to see if I can reset everything so that the computer can work well either wired or wireless. In the meantime, the blurex itself does its job nicely and gets a very good signal around the whole house.One thing I would ask of manufacturers, isn't there a way to make these range expanders so that they can either sit on a table or mount on the wall? In my setup, simply plugging into a wall outlet is not an option. Yes I could drape it over the top of a floor-mounted surge protector but that's not such a good idea since it's, ON THE FLOOR. I have it connected to an extension cord and have that sitting on top of one of my speakers in the living room but that's really not ideal since it can't stand up. If the thing has to be shaped the way it is, how about making some kind of caddye or cradle for it that I can affix to the wall so it will be vertical and be safely mounted? Just being designed to cover a whole wall socket is not very good, but then all these devices seem to be this way except some very expensive ones or ones that don't work very well. If anyone has other ideas or thoughts go ahead and write me outside of the review.Despite my griping as above, I'm not sorry I got the device, because it does well what it's supposed to, just wish instructions were better and its design was better. Still, it does work and you can't knock that...

For those who enjoy, or need, Ultra Wide Angle, such as for landscapes and architecture, or even for the real estate profession, there is a question that may pop up: is this lens really worth the money? And there is a quick one-word response: Yes!The 12-24mm is a DX format, not full frame. I shoot with DX, so this review is written from that perspective. The lens a very compact, yet a solidly built piece of glass. Yes it is primarily plastic with a metal mount, but it feels very good in your hands. And it performs! As many have said before me, cameras and lenses do not make a photographer, but, just as importantly, the right gear certainly assists the photographer do his/her job better.The focus on the 12-24mm is quite smooth throughout the short zoom range that it offers. And, even more important, it is tack sharp and provides excellent color contrast, even in many low-light situations. Architectural shots captured during moonlight are particularly nice. I have not experienced any hunting issues during focusing except on those rare occasions where there is virtually no contrast in the subjects in my vuiewfinder and there is very low light (which happens with virtually every lens).For wide-angle landscape images, the 12-24mm really delivers exceptional detail and clarity providing great depth. And after all, capturing shots that take your breath away (along with those others who view your work) is what it is all about.For real estate listings, this lens is an absolute winner. Being able to take in a whole room provides your prospective buyers with a much better idea of what you are offering them. In other words, it is light years ahead of a point-and-shoot or iPhone/Smartphone camera shot.At 12mm there are times of slight distortion or soft edges but not always, so some of that, particularly the distortion, may be my fault. I can live with that as I can improve my skills.As this lens uses 77mm filters I was lucky, in that my 18-300mm is also that size so I did not have to shell out more cash for those little critters.The fact that it is an f/4 fixed-aperture when one might want f/2.8 or f/3.5 might be a deal breaker for some. Not for me. I have no complaints with this feature. Yes, I toyed with the idea of the 10-24mm f/3.5-4.5 but, in the end I choose this baby and have no regrets.A word of caution...you probably cannot use your camera body's built-in flash or the dreaded dark shadow will appear in your image. Make sure you attach your Speedlight (or equivalent) during those times you need extra light.For landscape, architecture, and tight interior shots, this is the lens to get. I have used it on both a D90 and D5100 with outstanding results. Highly recommenmded.

Actually, I'm not a fan of O.C. but then extra bits of performance come with little or none price - why not to get them? I installed this CPU onASUS P8P67 PRO <REV 3.1>and using standard ASUS overclocking software was able to run CPU at 4.3Ghz. Wow! Never thought +30% of performance could be get so easy. I ran some stability tests and the systems didn't show any problem except CPU overheating which is expected since I use stock air cooler and radiator. Though, even with air cooling OC works fine since processor decreases speed when idle or under little loading. Even modern games don't load this processor to 100% so, overheating in the middle of a game is unlikely.Also I did some performance testing of my GTX295 and it shown a little performance boost comparing with the similar configuration built on 1th generation CPU/mobo. Boost is about 3-5% so, you probably won't notice it in games.Buying this CPU keep in mind that it has built-in RAM controller which limits your OC capabilities. One of the most noticeable ones is fixed DRAMM:FSB ratio which is 28:3. Because of this if you don't manually adjust settings your 2000Mhz RAM will run at 1866Mhz: 100Mhz FSB x 28/3 x 2 = 1866.6(6). I increased FSB to 107,1 to get best of my DDR3.

review_title: Nice Sound at a Reasonable Price
review_text: I am very pleased with my purchase of the Onkyo HT-S9100 THX.  I started my research with Consumer Reports, and I noted that Onkyo generally was at the top of their ratings, although this particular unit was not reviewed.  I searched online, and saw good reviews on Amazon.  I also found that the system was a top pick by Home Theater magazine.  It was delivered in just a few days at a time convenient for me.  (The delivery company called ahead of time.)  It came in a fairly big box (in good condition), but not as big as some online chatter led me to believe.  The box was heavy but I was able to move it around.  Set up was easy.  The instruction manual is clear.  The wiring was fine.  Some reviewers thought the wire should be upgraded to a higher grade, but they work fine for me as is.  I did have to buy some longer wires to get the wires to the rear speakers.  The room they are in is roughly 14 x 20.  I bought speaker wall brackets at [...] for about $5.00-$6.00 a unit, and they work well.  The speakers are very heavy for their size, and I think they would droop a bit, but since I angled down slightly towards the listening areas, they are OK.  I previously had a Sony home theater system that sold for about $900 in 2001.  I set up the two systems side by side (more or less.  I didn't actually place the Onkyo speakers in exactly the right spot, and I did not calibrate the system.)  I found an amazing difference in sound.  I listened to some jazz, and the piano and bass were very clear, almost like being at a live performance.  I played a Blu-Ray DVD (Avatar) and again was pleased with the surround sound.  The woofer was very nice.  I have set it at the THX setting.  Finally, I played the Master and Commander movie DVD.  At one point, the ship was creaking under the wind and currents, and I thought someone was trying to get into my house.  My family had a good laugh.  I am using the system with a Panasonic 50 inch plasma TV (G-20) and a Panasonic Blu-Ray DVD player (recommended again by Consumer Reports).  All in all, I am pleased with my purchase and enjoy the better surround sounds.  I'm sure you can find better and pay more, but for my budget, I think I got a good deal.

review_title: It's only flaw is being stuck using inferior software.
review_text: If I am going to be forced to use proprietary software for an audio and video player to work, it better be fantastic.  This "Songbird" is for the birds.  I must have installed and uninstalled and updated and repaired and downloaded again and etc. etc.  Importing media is a guessing game. You never know what it will like or spit back at you.  And then on the unit itself, it is just a mess.  Once you find the music you want, it might play.  I also notice music skipping and jumping quite a bit.  This could be from the shabby software trying to get it on the thing. Or it could just be the player.So why the generous three stars? Because with some technical knowledge and the ability to edit and convert files and actually rework the unit, it's just fine.  In other words, delete all the useless software.  Treat it as an external drive and create your own folders.  Name them Music, Video, Photos etc.  This is a lot of work with music, as you have to create folders for each artist.  So what I have done is dedicated the player to two artists "Keane" and "Jason Mraz", since I listen to them the most, I have over 500 tracks between the two of them, and then there are the music videos and concert footage. So it fills up pretty well.  But still keeping space for photos and taking photos or shooting video.I do not recommend deleting everything like I did, unless you want to take a chance.  I had nothing to lose.  The Songbird software is on the player itself.  There are no discs for your PC.  You plug it in your USB (with a really stupid combo AV cord) and the software should autorun... if not, go into it like an external drive and double click on "setup".  But, like I said, I deleted it from the device.  First of all, it's out of date in need of an update. So you just download the full version from the Songbird Phillips site.  Which I will try again maybe in the future.  But for now, my clearing it out works for me.  You don't lose menu control as once I deleted the files, I click the reset to factory settings, and it does not delete your files, it just organizes the menu.The camera and video capabilities are impressive for fun and party use only.  Not pro looking shots of anything.  Just stuff you can upload to facebook and youtube etc.  It's very light and the earphones have a nice fitting shape.  But, it's not an iPod or Flip Camcorder.  It's a combo of both, but cheaper.  But you get what you pay for.  [...]The biggest plus here is the microSD slot. Just put files directly on the card and then put in the player, and you can shoot the Songbird.

Unfortunately, since Bluray is still in its infancy (so-to-speak) there aren't many options for players.  I bought the BD-P1400 and found that while the picture quality is great and the upconversion quality is superb, there are still some problems with this player.  My first unit starting having hardware/software problems; namely, it would simply quit playing during the middle of the movie, at random times and multiple times throughout a movie.  I returned the unit and exchanged for the same model and have not experienced the same problem with the new unit.  Also, there are some basic functions missing on this player:1) No Replay/Skip-back button which seems to be a pretty standard feature on DVD players nowadays.  I miss this button a lot.2) No memory feature.  When you stop a movie you have to start over as if you just loaded it in the player.3) (2) becomes a very annoying problem if you pause movies frequently for breaks or doing chores around the house, which I do a lot.  When you pause a movie it will only pause for about 5 minutes, then it will go to screen saver.  After a few minutes of screen saver it will STOP the movie and when you come back you have to start the movie over and try to find where you were.  This is a MAJOR annoyance!4) It is missing DVD playback features like viewing different angles, etc.It is my opinion that this player was released prematurely based on its feature set. review_title: Pass on this Router.  Too Many Issues to Configure.
review_text: I purchased two of these and an Amped wireless access point for 2 of my customers to replace some old routers that died.  One was for a warehouse and the other a funeral home.  Both needed the extended range.  I decided to vary from my normal Asus NT12B router and give these a try.  To date, I have received 4 routers (2 original and 2 replacements) and all have the same issues.  If you change any of the default settings on the IP address page and admin password page, the units reboot automatically and will not come back online without power cycling the units.  This is after updating firmware and resetting to defaults.  Each time I give it a static IP and change the password, the router goes offline and requires it to be powered off and on.  If I put the defaults back in, it then will reboot and the page will refresh and re-appear staying online as it should.  This is not acceptable when I have to depend on the router as the gateway for my customer's network and uptime is critical.  Most home uses will probably not even notice this since most only plug them in and add a wireless SSID (how many home users still have admin/admin or other for your routers GUI access?).  Any variation from that could create downtime if the unit reboots.This router also claims a coverage of 10,000 sq. ft.  I found that claim to be marginal at best.  In an open warehouse, I get no better signal than the older wireless router that was there originally.  I also found that even though signal strength may show as high (150mbps), the signal quality was poor.  Lots of drops with data transfers that didn't occur with the previous equipment.Customer support was fine.  They were helpful, but could not resolve my issues after recommending I get replacement equipment.  It is not acceptable to have issues with manual configurations, especially when it deals with the access password.  I have spent hours troubleshooting to no avail and can not recommend this router for purchase.

review_title: Great product for what it is... understand what it isn't
review_text: Why are there so few dual monitor KVM's out there?I bought this and it works great, but you MUST understand that this KVM handles analog video signals ONLY.  If you have systems with dual vga ports, or a vga and DVI-I, or vga and DVI-A, you're fine because you can get a converter from DVI-I or DVI-A to vga/hd15 plug format to work with this.  If, on the other hand, you have something with DVI-D (such as dell docking stations that have dual DVI-D and a single vga) you are out of luck without an expensive digital-to-analog converter for the second monitor.  I had one of these and had to connect it directly to one of the monitors (bypass the kvm) which certainly works (occasionally have to manually select input on that monitor when you switch to that system using the kvm) but loses a little of the convenience you should have with this fairly expensive kvm.With that said, there aren't many options out there and this thing is small and build like a tank, very easy to use and works as advertised.  Particularly like the usb on the back to take your printer with you to each system as you switch... as well as the usb on the front for a thumb drive.UPDATE:One other option for an analog signal (necessary for this KVM) is if you have available DisplayPort interfaces (which I had 2 of on my Dell Docking Station).  Google it if your not familiar with it.  The bottom line is that, while this is a digital format, it was created with intent of being friendly toward legacy display formats.  In other words, you can buy a Display port to vga active converter for about $30.  The key here seems to be the word "active".  It's also very nice that this digital-to-analog conversion can be done with line power (no extra cords or bricks required).

The weakness of this system is in the limitations that it imposes on installation and the powerline over Ethernet setup.I understand the niche that Logitech is trying to serve, but unfortunately, it falls short for me.I need a good reliable, fully mounted, outdoor video system. The Logitech install doesn't allow for attic installation and an extension cord is not an option to mount the unit on the corner of my house.The main problem is that any security system is usually going to need to be mounted on the corner of a house or the corner of a building where an outlet (to connect the power) is no where to be found and is usually directly installed via the attic, or a high ceiling.These limitations make the camera more of a spot surveillance system instead of a dedicated serious unit.I would recommend a little more robust system for the money spent, if you are looking to simply spy on your teenage daughter and need a night vision camera that points in one direction, then this camera could fit the bill.The ability to record without the PC being on and the ability to stream to your iPhone make it a good teenager or simple spy camera to catch the neighbors dogs pooping in your lawn at night. In that regard, the software is really easy to use, the camera video quality is excellent, although night vision can be a little grainy ... I think this is due to a slightly underpowered IR light on the camera ....Other wise it is a solid build with easy hook up and directions. Logitech customer service has always been good (I did not need them for this product - but I have called them before for other things).If the camera had a more flexible install range - it would be a 4 star .... maybe 5 review.

Edit November 21, 2011I cannot believe I gave this tablet such a low rating! I originally had issues with the tablet cutting off randomly and not coming back on. I let my battery power run out, then charged it from dead on the computer. I did this for a week and after that my powering off issue has disappeared completely! I was searching the internet on my tablet and fell asleep. I usually wake up the next morning with a tablet that was shut off however it worked. In fact, it stayed on until the battery died and that took a few days to deplete. I am glad I didn't throw the towel in as I originally wanted to do. My only gripe is that I hate the stock browser so I installed Opera and it's awesome! I highly recommend this device!!! I have moved my rating from a 2 back to a 5!Edit August 23, 2011I have had this tablet for over a week. Throughout the ownership of this tablet the screen will dim out like normal and after it dims you can't turn the display back on. So, in order to remedy the issue you have to press and hold the power button until it powers all the way off then turn it back on. This has happened more than 26 times since I have owned it and this is irritating.Another irritation is that I tried to get support from Samsung on their website. I already have a Samsung account because I have the Galaxy S 4G and that's registered. I attempted to add this on the account. When I entered the serial number the model, P1010, shows up fine. However, when I try to submit the registration it keeps asking for the IMEI/HEX meaning the only model that is eligible for service and warranty is the 3G version (costs more and you have to have a data account opened at a cell phone company to operate it). This sounds like they are not going to be standing behind this product. Qik also does not work and never will because when you select the service it tells you that the service will be available soon but since Samsung does not appear to be updating the Wi-Fi version this app is never going to work.My last peeve with this device is that it is not going to be updated. The other tablets have been moved up to the 2.3 (Gingerbread) OS and this device is not eligible. I think this is not right and why would you put a device out that you intended to seal off from service, warranty and updates? This is very dishonest and I am starting to be sorry that I made the decision to get this one. I am not saying that I am going out and splurging on a device that is well over $600 but I think I am going to find another device that the creators stand behind. Maybe Motorola or Acer. For this reason, I have to move my rating down to 2 stars because while the device works most of the time, once cannot overlook the non-support of this device. The difference between HP and the Galaxy Wi-Fi is that the HP customers had no idea that service was going to be stopped for their device. Samsung knew and didn't say anything.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Original Review:Let me first explain something. I have a Samsung Galaxy S 4G. My phone does a lot and I never thought much of tablets. I thought tablets were a dumb waste of money because you have the internet on your phone, right? So why fiddle with a stripped down version of a phone that you can't make calls on if you don't open a separate account at a carrier? After quite a few months of this I decided to take a stab at a tablet. I figured this was a purchase that I can laugh about at a later date. Well, looks like tablets got the last laugh.I ordered this device yesterday and received it this afternoon. I received free overnight shipping because I am a Prime customer and the device was at a warehouse close to me which afforded me the luxury of no shipping charges. I was a little anxious to open the box because I just wanted to see what the fuss was about. I am a creature of screens. The bigger the screen, the happier I am as long as it's vivid. There is a 10.1 inch option but I felt that might be a little big for me and this 7 inch screen is perfect for me and very portable.What's in the box:- 16GB 7 inch Tablet- Data Cord- Wall Charging Jack- Samsung Ear Buds- Instruction ManualsInitial Setup:When I plugged the device in it was already 60% charged but I allowed it to charge all the way before I powered it on. When I turned it on it took about 45 seconds to power up to the initialization process. In this process you will enter your email accounts you want synced to the device as well as enter the information you need to log in to your WiFi. This process took me no more than about 5 minutes. After the process the tablet goes to the home screen. There are five home screens on this device, which in comparison my Galaxy S 4G has seven.Space:When I looked at the amount of space on the device through the settings I found that out of 16GB there was 12.60GB available for use. That's enough for me for now however if you think you will be adding more media than 12GB then please invest in a micro SD card. This device has an expandable slot and as far as I know cannot read cards over 32GB. I have no issues with this for now but I will buy a card later if I need more space, though I am not sure why I would.Screen:The screen is very large and crisp. I did not find any pixelation and that's a relief. The glare can be a bit annoying, but no more annoying than my cell so it's bearable for me however if glare is an issue then you might want to seek a different device because you can get past a lot of discrepancies in a device but you can't ignore a screen.Operating System:The operating system on this device is the Android 2.2 Froyo. This is an operating system that was designed for the Android cell phones and not necessarily a tablet. I have not had any issues operating this device under the Froyo, however the most recent release is Honeycomb which is the operating system designed specifically for tablets. This device, being the WiFi version, is not going to upgrade to the Honeycomb operating system. When I plugged the device in to the Kies software (will explain what that is a little later) and looked at the firmware I noticed that there was a message that the firmware could not be updated. If updating to Honeycomb is important to you then you may want to look at a device that is going to be updated, have it already pre-installed or root this device and install the operating system yourself. There are many instructions on the internet on how to do this. I am content with the operating system and do not plan on doing it so I will not be updating with any information about how to install that.WiFi:I chose to use my cell phone as an access point for my tablet because this maintains the stability of always being connected to the internet whereas connecting to my home WiFi means that when I leave to go to work the connection obviously drops. If you are one of the lucky few to have Mobile AP in your wireless settings then you should be able to use that connection to connect the tablet and 4 other wireless devices to your internet network. Before doing so, make sure you have an unlimited data plan because this tablet can use a lot of data without you even realizing it and the tablet along with your cell using the same data package and not having unlimited spells impending doom for your bill due to overages.It was very easy to set up the WiFi. When you first turn the device on you set the connection before it takes you through the process of retrieving email from the accounts you choose. I ran into no issues when setting this up.Bluetooth:I have not attempted yet to use Bluetooth on this device because I have to be honest, I am not sure what Bluetooth means on a tablet. I mean, I have a Bluetooth I use on the cell but that's for phone calls. I will tamper with that later and see what develops, then I will report back on what that feature does exactly.Internet Browser:This is one of the main reasons for getting a tablet, so having a browser that works is definitely necessary. The browser is great! The flash works just fine. I have not gone to a site that does not work yet. I went to Phone Dog's website and looked at a video  and that worked. I went to a few news sites and looked at video's in the browser and it worked fine. I also tried Gilmore Girls at The WB's website and that worked awesome as well. This is definitely a full browser. Is it perfect? No. However it is close enough for me and at this price you can't really find much to complain about.Music Entertainment:In order to move music to this player, you need to download Samsung Kies. Kies is the software that finds updates for this device as well as allow you to sync media. I found that this was very easy to get used to. The first thing I was thinking was that I was going to have to find a DRM remover to decode my music because I use Zune Marketplace and like ITunes, their music is DRM protected which usually prevents you from syncing to any other device that is not designated to the software. Imagine my surprise when I tested a music file and was able to play it on this device without any obscure messages! This is the first time in history that has happened and I am glad I decided to try it before I paid 19.99 for the software to remove the protection. The songs sound great on headphones but the speakers on this device could be louder in my opinion, but not a total let down for me because I always have ear phones plugged in. I have not had any issues with the music. To download Kies software you can go to Samsung's website and download it from there. Last time I was on the site they had an outdated version for download however when it downloads it will update automatically so that shouldn't be an issue.Video EntertainmentI have a myriad of movies on my computer and 1TB removable hard drive. Most of my movies are .avi but I do have a few .divx and .mp4 movies as well and they have all played. Now, when I attempted to add the first movie to the device it stopped me and asked to download a codec packet so it would work. That process took less than a minute and I have not gotten any messages since then. The movies are not in HD so the quality is not as crisp as I would like however it's sufficient for me. For best results it may be better to try a HD video. I will find one and report back on how that makes a difference, if it does.Marketplace:The Android Marketplace comes pre-installed on the device. Please take note that there are some apps that will not operate on this device because it's not compatible. I am not sure how many apps but I guess trial and error is the only way to find out. I have noticed that there is no app that supports Facebook or Facebook chat as of yet so if that's important you may want to take note that no tablet has a designated Facebook app as of yet, the way I hear it. I do have Tweet Deck which allows me to still update my Facebook status and Twitter status with no issues. You can connect to all social networking sites by going through the browser. I tried Netflix because that was an important app to me and it worked for me without a hitch, much to my delight. I have been able to download and install a live wallpaper as well with no issues.Another reason for this purchase is the Kindle app. I am an avid reader, especially at work in my downtime, and I wanted to make sure that this app worked. The Kindle app is already installed on this device when you get it and all you have to do is log in with your amazon email address and password. The screen is perfect for reading and I have already enjoyed reading a few chapters of Nora Roberts "Key of Valor" which I purchased from the Kindle app store.I did purchase a cover to go with this device from amazon as well and it closes and clips like a book and I love it. The cover is called Case Crown Faux Leather Premium Case and it was $20.18. The exterior is really soft but sturdy and the interior is a black crushed velvet. It really is nice and compliments the device well. All in all I am glad I made the splurge and I would recommend this to anyone who is looking for an inexpensive tablet that does more than half of what the more expensive tablets does. I look forward to exploring a little more with this device and as I find more discoveries I will update this review as always. Happy purchasing!

review_title: Some interesting features, but directions are dodgy
review_text: I'm comparing this to my first GPS, a Tomtom XXL with traffic, which also came from the Vine program. This Magellan model doesn't have traffic sensing which IMO is vital if you live in a busy metropolitan area where your route and ETA can be greatly affected by traffic. But they have other models that include traffic, so I won't downgrade it for that. Both this and the Tomtom are pretty stripped-down, starter units.This GPS seems to emphasize POIs (points of interest, like stores and restaurants) more than anything. It breaks them down into categories and sub categories and even has a AAA ratings guide gimmick - for instance, find a AAA rated restaurant near you. When you're out on the highway, you can press an icon (actually it may be safer to have a passenger do it) and see a list of restaurants, gas stations and lodging at the nearest exit. Also if you look up POIs near you, the list indicates with arrows which direction they are from you - the Tomtom doesn't do this, so you have to try to figure out if that restaurant is on your way to your destination or behind you.I also like the address book feature, and the one-touch menu. With the address book, you can enter names, phone numbers, email addresses, and even group them into categories like relatives, coworkers, etc. With the one-touch menu, just press one icon in the corner and press a button for home, the nearest gas or ATM or any button you assigned to your favorites. The Tomtom makes you go through a couple of menus to access favorites. The Magellan mount is also much better than the Tomtom mount which is awful (I bought an aftermarket mount for it).Where this falls short, is what a GPS is supposed to do well: directions. First, when I turn it on, it takes several minutes to pick up the signal, then it starts showing and reading directions from where I started off! And if I'm parked in my driveway, it'll tell me to turn onto the street that's behind my backyard (?). A couple of times, it strangely said "perform a U turn" when I was going straight and in the right direction. Roundabouts seem to get it confused. There's only one voice, a tinny robotic "female" voice (Tomtom has several voices available in its unit, with more voices downloadable). The signal can be slow to keep up with you, and it needs better graphics because sometimes it's hard to tell if a turn is coming up because a large yellow arrow obscures the green on the road ahead. The software is super slow (I have Windows 8) and ancient-looking, and I couldn't update any POIs on it.I don't think I would recommend this GPS when there are other, more accurate ones in this price range.

review_title: Solid.  Functional.  Good for travel.  Not the best for video, but good enough.
review_text: "3-Way Fluid Pan Head" implies video.  That's mostly what I do.  I have a nice heavy tripod with a true fluid head.  I don't think anything under 10 pounds will ever compete in this arena.  When it comes to video tripods, heavy is good.  So when I bought this as a light weight video tripod, I knew it would be inferior to my other sticks.  For still photography this tripod is outstanding.  Fully functional, easy to use - although at 7 pounds, it's pretty heavy for just still work.  For video, it's okay.  The horizontal pan is not great, but manageable.  I've taken it apart to try and get the right tension on the panning.  The "fluid" comes from the grease that is squished between the plates in the axle of the head.  I don't know how this will hold up long term.  I have visions of repacking bicycle bearings.  I have not been able to adjust it to the sort of sweet spot that other tripods offer.  I use a really nice (and old) Davis and Sanford set up at work.  This one does not compare.  Still, this tripod is very solid, and at this price and moderate weight, it's exactly the sort of sticks you might put on a plane for a vacation to the beach.  Short horizontal pans are okay, and it's pretty easy to lug around and set up static shots.  I should point out that the vertical pan is not very good at all, and dynamic shots that include both horizontal panning and vertical panning are going to be very difficult with these sticks.  Maybe if you load it down with sandbags, but unweighted you'll be unhappy with complex pans.The handles make putting it in and out of the bag a problem, and two of the three must be removed to fully pack it away.  I guess this isn't that big of a deal, but even my big old 20 pound studio monster tripod is easier to pack up.  The bag that comes with it is fine.My only real complaint is the single release plate.  I own several tripods, and use a bunch more at work.  This release plate is unique (in my experience). This tv has an absolutely stunning picture! We have really enjoyed this television over the last few weeks! My kids watch Netflix and YouTube, and play video games on this tv, and it has been superb, and we've all watched cable tv on it as well.Set up was easily handled by my husband and 12 year old son (husband also liked the packing the tv comes in). We have wifi, but in the interest of the best possible connection, we have the tv wired directly to the internet. Setting up the picture was very easy as well--there are pre-set selection and if course, you can adjust them as need for your particular environment. Our living room is fairly dim in the Spring/Summer months due to the many trees around our home, and we lie to watch it in a fairly dim room anyway. My husband feels the screen is a little reflective, but in a darker room, it really isn't a problem.This Smart tv comes with a pretty cool little remote, very much like a Wii remote--you shake it to wake it up and use the cursor to move and click on things on the screen. Another really cool feature is you can "talk" to the remote: press the microphone button and you can tell the tv what you want to do. "She" will look up something on the internet or pull up a channel or show for you. This is a very cool feature, my husband and son really love this. They talk to her more than they talk to me! (The tv is represented by a cute red headed girl avatar who appears in the screen.) Very nice tv for checking out stuff on YouTube, recipes, etc. It's amazing how often you can think of something and easily connect to the internet on this tv!The tv offers a bunch of apps for Hulu, Netflix, games, etc., and honestly, we haven't even explored everything it has to offer yet! My teenage daughters love Netflix, and the tv has been in use nearly every evening. You can also hook up your smart phone to the tv and download your videos and phones wirelessly! I discovered that by accident when I walked in to the room and they started communicating (just turn off that setting on your phone to stop this interactive feature).I'm sorry to say this tv doesn't come with even an inexpensive pair of 3D glasses, which would have been lovely. At this time, we still haven't obtained those, and I think you need the more expensive )active" glasses for the plasma 3D rather than the "passive' ones you'd get in the movie theater (although I personally, am not above trying any 3D glasses). A relative near by also has a 3D projector tv, so she has offered to loan me some 3D movies, so we will try to check out this feature some time over the summer, and I promise to update then.Another happy feature of this tv is it has pretty good sound! Our last two LED tvs had terrible sound, and while we hooked up speakers to this one anyway, since that's what we have in our living room already, we could have done fine without external speakers. There are also 3 HDMI hookups, which is great if you want to hookup your laptop or tablet and stream movies. I can't imagine you'd need more than three. There is also an a component hookup, an AV hook up and also an optical hook up (and that's where my husband has our stereo are plugged in). The remote control is also programmable to the components, so we can control the cable and the stereo (speakers) with it, which is very nice.There are a lot of features to explore in this tv, and I really feel like we've barely scratched the surface (especially me, since I can barely prey the remote away from my husband and son! They LOVE this television!). If you have the money to spend, and are in the market for a Smart TV, I would definitely recommend this one. I've never used any LG products before I was exposed to their tvs, but I have great confidence in LG now, they make an excellent and fairly easy to use product. Like all Smart products, using them is intuitive and takes a short time to "learn," but if you have kids (ESPECIALLY if you have kids!), they will be running with this remote in no time flat! I'm really thrilled with the gorgeous picture, it makes watching any HD tv shows or movies a pleasure!

review_title: A CB antenna that does the job.
review_text: Even though I am a ham radio guy I was into CB first starting in the 1970's.  CB is great in the car for traffic reports on channel 19 as long as those riding with you can put up with the trash mouths in between the road reports. I use this antenna on the trunk of my car attached to the radio of the day, either a classic Robyn SB-510D SSB rig or a Bearcat 980 SSB. Both radios work well with this antenna. SWR is below 1.5:1 on all channels. Fit and finish is better than other mag mount antennas in the food chain. The soft plastic sheet under the magnet also covers the lip of the plastic around the magnet so less chance of scratching the paint. The antenna is longer than what I am used to. It will not clear the garage door without stuffing it into the trunk. Not a big deal for me but for some could be an issue.. but a long antenna to me means there is more antenna to get a decent signal out and into the radio, which is a good thing. I'm not sure if the plastic over the loading coil will hold up to long term outdoor use. It feels like something I would use indoors, not outdoors, but time will tell on that one. No problems making contacts with local base stations 10 -15 miles away on SSB while driving down the road using stock power. I will update this review after I use it for a few months. 73.

I had just purchased a samsung 40" lcd tv in Jan of 06 and was very excited about seeing my movies on this screen, as everyone all discovered, regualar dvds...look like cr_p on even the best progressive dvd players, which I felt I owned with my faroudja powered phillips dvd player.  I loved this phillips dvd player and it literally smoked on quality of viewing of them over my old high end sony, but with the new advances in lcd tv's, phillips failed miserably and then knew, this was not going to work so I needed to solve problem pronto...I started investigating the hd players but figured we were a few years away before they all got the bugs worked out.  While shopping for a new player..I stumbled on upscalers. I did my typical obsessesive research on these machines, including calling Oppo and even Samsung. I originally was holding out for Samsung hd1080 which was announced a year ago last january on the big show in vegas every year.  The announcement was the hd1080 by sumsung would be released in april of 2006, but nada, in fact they cancelled the release completely of that dvd player, so I went with the 2nd best offering of the hd960, which was pretty similar in features.  Anyway..with all the reserch, I picked the samsung over the oppo after speaking to both compaines directly.  At first I was disappointed with the Samsung and wanted to return it, but after a little playing around and a weeks use of it, it got better.  True...no hdtv, but at times it looks pretty close to identical at times.  Quality of dvd's also play a big part on the ability to produce a better picture.  In other words, not all dvd's will look great because they didn't have much quality to begin with, but will look pretty good and definitley better with this player.  If you are semi dvd collector like me, and really don't want to give up your collection, then I highly suggest you think about the Samsung hd960, I don't think you can go wrong. I did experience some peculiar blinking when I was using an average brand optical, but when I went strickly hdmi...it was flawless. review_text: The latest earphones I am reviewing are the Sennheiser CX680 Sports Earbuds which the company are working with Adidas that offer:*  Sweat and water-resistant ideal for sports*  Earfin holding system secure and comfortable fit during workouts*  High-output ear-canal drivers energizing sound and superb noise insulation*  DuPont Kevlar cable, superior strength and durabilityPackaged with the earbuds are rubber black earfins (Small, Medium and Large), housing covers, ear adapters (S, M, L), volume control/extension cable, storage pouch, cable clip and cleaning tool.I.  FIRST GLANCESennheiser is a pretty solid company that is known for many products.  In first glance of the CX 680, you kind of hope there are other colors available aside from fluorescent green/yellow but for the most part, it is visible and if you have it in your gym bag, you can easily spot it.  Love the fact that for its pricepoint, you do get multiple ear buds, adapters and housing covers but I have to give Sennheiser a major thumbs up because I have reviewed more expensive earbuds that give you the extra ear buds but that's it.  So, you're getting extra accessories, especially the extension cable/volume control was a nice addition and you can keep everything in its black Sennheiser pouch. From US rock, hip hop, pop, jazz, classical, French Pop, J-Pop, K-Pop, etc. while working out on the bike.  Bass comes out quite clearly but as does treble.  Tried various settings on my iPod and also tested it on a SanDisk Sansa and the quality was fantastic!When I read one reviewer mention the "tinny sound", I at first was wondering if I had the same problem but then I realized, I was wearing them improperly and adjusting it in my ears, then I was able to get strong bass.So, not sure if the reviewer used the different earbuds or did any repositioning but one I did it, the tinny sound was replaced with solid bass.III. DURABILITYWhen I saw the mention of Kevlar, I was amused.  What is the kevlar made for and you learn it's with the cables.  For anyone who has used earbuds, even with major companies, there were times that I would get frustrated with problems with a wire and would have to bend the wire to make them work.  So, its great to see Sennheiser going the extra step in using Dupont Kevlar for their cables.I tested the various earbuds and fins, and no problems.  I've read one reviewer who had broken her fins, while you do get multiple fins (S, M, L), not sure how they broke because they are durable unless you are trying to stretch them out.  But because Sennheiser is a well-known company, I'm sure one can easily contact customer service for additional accessories.JUDGMENT CALL:As mentioned, I have reviewed several earbuds, expensive earbuds and these are probably one of the better ones I have reviewed that not only produce great sound, come with multiple accessories and extras that many other expensive big brands don't even offer.  As mentioned, there are are some good brands that I have used that failed, especially with its cable after using it.  While I don't know how long these Kevlar cables last, the fact that Sennheiser has used Kevlar for their cable is actually a big thumbs up for me and shows me that they are trying to address quality issues that people have had with earbuds.While, I could go for a different color than fluorescent early '90s Bodyglove colors, I can easily recommend these earbuds.  Once again, I personally don't think these fins can easily be busted unless one was stretching them too hard and as for the tinny sound, at first I experienced them until I repositioned to find that "sweet spot" and my perspective changed for these earbuds. They sound great on my iPod and Sansa and tried various styles of music with different EQ settings and the CX680 were quite solid.Sure, there is a lot of competition out there for earbuds but if you want to get your money's worth, the Sennheiser CX680 is definitely worth it!

Set her to infinity, point at the sky or landscape (or hyperfocal focus) and you're ready to shoot without even worrying. Why get this lens? For sky shots and landscapes. It also works really well in doors, if you want to take photos of the entire room and everyone in it, at close quarters. It's f2.8 lets you really do well in low light without a flash if you wish. review_title: The best Netbook out there right now!!
review_text: After my laptop suddenly died recently, I needed a new portable computer, and fast.  I did some pretty extensive online research and decided to take the risk on a Netbook (risk because it's so different and so small!)  I have never looked back.  I've had it for 2 months now, and am nothing but ecstatic with my little Samsung.  Always had Dell or HP in the past, but Samsung is starting to make me a believer.  Though they seem to be new to the computer world, I think this Netbook is the best one out there, and here's why:1.  The keyboard is almost full size.  One of the (big) drawbacks to netbooks is the tiny keyboards, which make it difficult to type.  Can be very annoying if you use it for an extended period of time.  After I brought my Samsung on vacation with my family recently, they all loved it so much that my dad and my niece went out and bought netbooks.  However, they made the mistake of going with the Acer -- a much smaller keyboard.  My dad is becoming quite frustrated with it.  And supposedly the Samsung has an antibacterial coating on the keyboard.  Not sure if it actually does anything, but nice to know it's there...2.  Upgrading the RAM is so easy a caveman could do it.  haha  Seriously, though, it seems like all netbooks come with 1GB of RAM.  If you can find one with 2GB you probably pay through the nose.  You can buy a 2GB card for between $20-$30.  There are lots of guides online, but in 2min you can basically pop out the old and pop in the new, simply using a regular screwdriver.  It's that easy and you now have 2GB RAM.  I did it soon after buying it, though, so I'm not sure if there's a big difference or not.  It is fast though!3.  It has Win XP.  If you're like me and find Vista to be way too unstable for an OS, there are few choices out there.  Hopefully Samsung doesn't decide to "upgrade" their OS.4.  Built in webcam.  I don't use it much, but when I'm traveling (which is why I bought it) it's nice to be able to video chat with the family.5.  Lots of peripheral plug ins.  Unlike the Mac Air (which I had strongly considered despite it's ridiculous price tag) this has 3 USB ports, a VGA (for a monitor/TV), ethernet, headphone, speaker, and of course power cord.6.  In addition it also has a card reader!  I think it only takes SD but that works for me!7.  Extremely long battery life.  I can go about 8hrs on one charge.  Haven't really had to try it (have always been near an outlet), but there are NO WORRIES about the battery on this thing.  Better performance than my Dell laptop!  There are several settings so you can easily change from a power save mode (turn off wifi, screen dimmer) to high performance mode.  I usually just leave it in high performance and can still leave it unplugged for much of the day.With all those pros, there were a couple of cons:1.  No optical drive.  However, if you're shopping for netbooks, you've realized that none of them have an optical drive.  That's how they make it so small.  You can either buy an external one or, what I did, network your netbook to your home computer and use IT'S optical drive.  A nice solution!2.  When I was shopping the biggest con I saw was the mouse.  Yes it's small, but it's not that big of a deal.  I've quickly adjusted.  Every once in a while my finger runs off the top or something, but it's really not that big of a deal.  There's still a scrollbar on the side, a big mouse button across the bottom (press on the right or left for different buttons), and I think it's just the right amount of flush-ness with the case (looks nice!).  There's even some feature that I keep finding (still not exactly sure what the combo is to get it) that will change the text size of the page you're reading with just some swiping of fingers on the mousepad.  Kinda fun if you know how to do it...3.  Price.  As netbooks go this might be a little up there.  I paid just under $500 for the netbook, other decent ones go for as little as $200.  I think this one was worth the money though if you plan on using it a significant amt.4.  Size.  I initially was looking for a really tiny computer that I could stick in my purse and take with me, but would still be big enough to use.  Though this is the biggest of the netbooks out there, it still fits in one of my purses (a slightly oversized purse, but not a shoulder bag).  I just throw it in the little case it comes with (really just to protect from scratches -- it's a felt cover) and stick it in my purse.  Came in EXTREMELY handy while on vacation recently, and even just going around town to coffee shops etc.  Now that I have it, I can't imagine having a smaller computer.  The screen would probably be unbearable, not to mention the keyboard.5.  The case it comes with isn't very durable.  I thought this would be a drawback, but really it's not a big deal.  I found that sticking it in my purse without the felt cover left some little black scratches on the cover (I think from my keys rubbing on it).  But what kind of damage are you trying to protect it from?  I thought about buying a more substantial case, but realized i can just stick it in my purse or shoulder bag, and not much would happen to it.  Not a big drawback...I hope this thorough review is helpful to someone out there.  I was very grateful for all the reviews I read when I was shopping.  It was a tough choice between the Acer, Wind, and ASUS.  In the end, I am EXTREMELY happy with the Samsung and would highly recommend the Samsung.  I've played around with my dad's Acer a little, and find my Samsung to be quieter (fan almost never turns on and it's always cool!), bigger keyboard, and faster.  Slightly bigger screen is a little nicer too.  And if you're debating about color (like I was) seriously consider the white.  I was a little nervous about the white (just didn't seem like a white computer would look right) but it looks very sharp.  It's a matte finish and looks very new age and high tech.  Every time I pull it out (in class, in a coffee shop, or even in a restaurant once) I get tons of compliments and questions.  A very handy machine that I would buy again in a heartbeat!I don't work for Samsung or get a kickback or anything (though I wish I did!) but just love this computer and had a tough time shopping around and making a decision.  I'd be happy to answer any questions you have about it.PS -- if you're a new shopper to Amazon, I highly recommend ordering from Amazon.  Free shipping, and with the "5-9 day" option, I got it in 3 days, like most of my amazon purchases.  Great shipping and easy shopping!UPDATE 2/2013: 5 years old and still going strong!  No problems in this little guy. I've formatted and reinstalled windows a few times along the way to keep it speedy, but otherwise is wonderful!

review_title: Easy to configure, install, and use -- and most importantly, effective
review_text: I purchased this product for use in my entertainment center, which is really more like a large TV stand with enclosed compartments for various devices.  As usual, the cutouts in the back are too small to facilitate good airflow for hotter and more sensitive devices (such as the DVR, Xbox 360, and PS3).  Simply to protect the lifespan of these very devices, it's critical to ensure good airflow and ventilation if you have them enclosed.This fan is a great option.  Not only is it relatively powerful for its size, it's also fairly quiet (especially when enclosed in a television stand or entertainment center), easy to install, and painless to adjust.  The velocity knob is mounted on the fan enclosure itself, which is remarkably convenient.  In addition, the fan comes affixed to a small metal stand which makes mounting it to the case unnecessary.  It's simply sitting behind my DVR on the upper shelf of a bilevel compartment in my TV stand, and it works wonders to funnel the hot air from both Xbox 360 and DVR out the back.Finally, the cord design is also convenient.  The fan charges via USB, which might originally seem troublesome, but isn't bad at all once you realize that any universal AC/USB adapter can be used to plug it into a wall socket (such as those used for mobile phones or even the Amazon Kindle).  Plus, the cord is retractable, with a generous length but also a helpful solution for the usual menagerie of cables and cords that hide behind such entertainment centers.  The fan even comes with a two-year warranty.All in all, there isn't much *not* to like about this product.  I would and probably will buy again for the other side of my stand!

Once you're online with it, you have to have some very intimate knowledge of port forwarding within your router to receive the email notices of alarms.  This isn't easy.  The sensitivity settings aren't consistent from camera to camera, tons of false settings.  If someone runs by it, you get a blur.  The camera itself may be outdoor rated, but the cords, the antenna and the power supply module are not.  All will need to be routed into your home or a secure housing of some type.  They don't disconnect so you have to make some overly large holes in whatever you need to route it through.  I purchased 4 cameras and even with all the tricks of setting up, they appear to work well for a couple weeks.  One day, one of the simply would not connect to the wifi.  Unplug and reset/reboot per tech support instructions, nothing.  Had to climb up 18ft on a ladder to uninstall and use patchcord directly into the router, still nothing.  Camera appears to have failed.  2nd camera works but will not trigger on motion, rendering it useless unless you want to constantly monitor it.  Tried all the tricks through tech support again and still nothing.  In both cases they remote connect into your system to try and help which is great but ultimately they couldn't.  I have a 3rd camera that is stuck in IR mode, meaning that even in the daytime, it now only does black/white video and snap shots.  Tech support again tried to help but couldn'somewhat pleased with their indoor pan/tilt type cameras but they seem to oscillate in IR mode around dusk each day making an audible clicking noise.  They also very often can be beaten by simply moving past it quickly.  It either misses the shot completely or you get a blur.  All the settings have been changed by tech support to improve this but they could only make it slightly better.  All in all, ok toys but not serious security cameras.  Spend a little more from a better known and more reputable company.  It's a shame too, because their tech support people do work very hard to help you and they stay on the phone as long as you need them to.

review_title: Mediocre at best but nice to have wall mount option
review_text: When our DVD player died we went looking for something more than just a DVD player.  We wanted a sound bar with DVD and WIFI but quickly realized that we'd have to spend more than we paid for our TV for something like that.  So we settled on no sound and got this instead.  We have the matching Samsung TV and on the wall these two units look slick!We bought it at Best Buy for much less than listed here and because we wanted the option to return it easily to a store if we weren't satisfied.  We were very skeptical but gave it a try.We've now owned it for 6 months and must say aside from a few quirks that we'd improve about it we definitely love it.PROS:1 - Easiest setup - We brought this home, my husband connected it to the TV, put in the USB for WIFI and within 20 minutes we were up and ready to go.  Loved that!2- Quick & Easy WIFI - You need to insert the USB WIFI that comes in the box to the side of the unit so there's a USB stick coming off the side but it's not a big deal.  The WIFI connected right away to our home wireless internet without any issues and has been working great ever since.  There have been shows where resolution was very high and it sometimes disconnects from the internet since we are using wireless.  This is unavoidable I think as this even happens to your laptop sometimes while running wireless.  The unit is very smart though it stops the show, lowers the resolution and restarts it.  Sure, downfall is that you're watching it at a lower resolution but at least it doesn't hang up or not work at all and you can still watch your show.3 - Goodies inside - The units start up screen has Netflix, Pandora, YouTube, and Blockbuster.  If you have a NETFLIX account you will be able to watch anything on your instant watch queue.  You still have to go through the DVDs in the mail for those that are not on your instant queue so Netflix is halfway there but not fully. The way BLOCKBUSTER works is that you subscribe to Blockbuster In-Demand.  It's just like having In-Demand on your TV.  If you don't have a Blockbuster account you can just subscribe for free with no monthly charge.  The way it works is basically all the new releases and all of Blockbusters inventory that you find in the store is basically available here.  So if you want to watch a movie you pay the rental fee and watch it instantly without every having to go to the store again.  YouTube is self explanatory, you can watch any YouTube video through your TV.  If you have an account you can save videos as well.  For Pandora you will need an account - free - and can listen to an endless number of songs.  You can create stations and rate right through your TV.4 - Connectivity with Samsung TV - It's nice to have a Samsung TV with this unit as they seem to read each other very well.  Turn on the unit and no need to do anything with the TV, it turns on and changes input based on what you're going to watch.  Plus you can use one remote for both.5 - Bluray - For the price you get all these features and BluRay, a good selling point.CONS:1- Internet connectivity can stop sometimes as mentioned before if you are using wireless2 - A person peeve I have with this machine is that it's set to read DVD first so if you have a DVD in the player as soon as you turn it on it goes to play the DVD.  You have to eject every time or just not leave a DVD in there.  Would have made more sense on Samsungs part if it always went to the welcome screen and an option on there was to switch to DVD.  Maybe the next gen...Overall, for what we paid this is an excellent unit.  It was the cost of a BluRay DVD player but with the added bonus of WIFI and wall mount.EDIT - 2 YEARS LATER:After two years of using this and assessing it, I would now give it 2.5 stars.  It's wireless wifi connects 6 out of 10 times and out of those 6 times half of the time it has to stop and resume during movies.  We finally got the Apple AV cable and now just watch netflix without any interruptions that way making this now a very expensive dvd player for us.  With Blu Ray disks you need to be careful as it seems to take 10 minutes just to load the movie.  The mounting is still great as it looks great on the wall under our Samsung TV but that's pretty much the only pro to this unit.

review_title: I upgraded my HTCT100 and couldn't be happier - expansive sound, easy setup, and great price - Bluetooth a major bonus as well
review_text: Premium television sets used to advertise their screen size, image sharpness, and sound quality.  Not any more.  When you buy the latest LG, Sony, or any other LCD, LED, or Plasma display, the speakers are always on the back and very tinny with little bass response.  In short, the television manufacturers do not expect you to actually use the speakers in the TV.  Many diehard audiophiles will decide to spend hundreds or even thousands of dollars on stereo receivers hooked up to surround sound speakers.  For those with lots of money, space, and the time to set it up, these home theaters can be great.  For the rest of us, we want quality sound from our televisions that is compact and easy to setup.  This is the place where the Sound Bar really shines.There are many brands with some similarities - you typically get a long speaker to go under the TV itself, either on its own stand or mounted on the wall.  There is also a separate sub-woofer for deep noise response.This Sony HTCT260 was an upgrade to my existing Sony HTCT100.  Despite similar names, they are quite different.  To start, the Sony HTCT100 was a total of 250W of sound - three 50W speakers in the bar and a 100W subwoofer.  The Sony HTCT260 is 300W - two 85W front speakers and a 130W subwoofer.  Whether the front is two or three speakers is immaterial - they are all inside a single bar.The Sony HTCT100 had a subwoofer that plugged into the wall, and the audio from the source plugged into the subwoofer.  Then the Sound Bar plugged into the subwoofer with a proprietary cable.  That meant the subwoofer had to be near the sound bar.  However, it also meant that the subwoofer was a receiver in itself, with HDMI pass thru, analog input, and optical input.  HDMI pass-thru means you can plug your Blu-Ray player into the subwoofer, and then plug the subwoofer into the TV.  It had multiple HDMI inputs so the Sony HTCT100 could switch between sources.The Sony HTCT260 does away with the HDMI select capability - in fact, it doesn't have HDMI input at all, and the inputs are on the sound bar, not the sub-woofer.  The sub-woofer is a remote wireless device, so it can be placed anywhere, a major bonus.  It is shorter than the HTCT100 subwoofer, despite being more watts, is easier to conceal.  The only inputs are on the bar itself, consisting of Analog, Coaxial, and Optical.  Why did they make this change?  Consider my use of the HTCT100.  When I bought a TV that had networking capability, it meant that half the time I was using my TV, it was for content from the TV itself.  Since my TV had lots of HDMI inputs, it meant every device could also plug into the TV.  I eventually stopped using the HDMI passthrough and just plugged the optical out from my TV into the HTCT100.Since I assume most people have similar televisions now, the removal of the HDMI inputs and the wireless subwoofer of the HTCT260 makes sense.In terms of style, the sound bar is sharp looking, a little longer and wider than the HTCT100, and with a built-in display, it looks really good in my TV setup.  There are touch sensitive input select and volume buttons on the front, so you can adjust it even if you lose the remote control.Most important, how does it sound?  In a word, amazing.  I was dubious that the extra 50W would mean anything, but I found the sound far more immersive and expansive than with the HTCT100.  Previously on the HTCT100, I had actually hit the MAX and still thought the sound was too quiet for some sources, but now I can crank up the volume and actually get it too loud.  The bass is full and can be felt, but is not overpowering.  Simple "sound field" buttons on the remote allow you to adjust the effect for movies, games, or music.  With the subwoofer placed in the back of the room, I can achieve most of the surround sound effect without having to run wires and place tons of speakers.Finally, pairing the speaker with my iPhone via Bluetooth couldn't be simpler.  I hit "Pairing" on the remote, and about 30 seconds later I was blasting Tchaikovsky through the speakers from the iPhone.Highly recommended - I'm sure you could get better sound with a more expensive system, but bang for the buck, I am totally happy with this sound bar and highly recommend you get one to go with your new television set.

My computer hasn't been upgraded much since I built it a few years ago. When I built it, I decided to go with integrated network adapters and audio. My aBit motherboard's onboard audio was a reasonably good Realtek HD audio chip so I was content to stick with it rather than buying a discrete audio card, like I'd done in all of my previous builds. I decided the convenience of having integrated components was worth the small sacrifice in quality.About a year ago, I started using headphones heavily on my PC and became dissatisfied with the noisy onboard audio. I thought the best way to resolve this was to get an external USB DAC/headphone amp. While I got amazing sound, it wasn't quite as convenient as I expected it to be and decided a discrete audio card was probably my best choice. I settled on the Asus Xonar DX PCI Express card.PROS:- Stellar 116 dB SNR for front audio ports (112 dB for rear)- Front panel header- Dolby Pro Logic IIx and Dolby Headphone support- Low profile bracket included in addition to regular height- Great sound quality via a pair of Cirrus Logic DAC'sCONS:- Requires floppy-style Molex 4-pin connector for power- Does not autodetect headphone insertion- Software-based EAX 5.0 supportI badly wanted to get anASUS Xonar Essence STX Card, or comparable card with a built-in headphone amp and very high quality DAC. Unfortunately, I found it hard to justify parting with $200. I then narrowed my choices down to the more affordable options of the Asus Xonar DX and theCreative Labs X-Fi Titaniumcards. When I found out that the X-Fi Titanium didn't include support for front-panel headers, it was an easy choice. Besides, the Xonar DX had a better rated SNR (116dB front/112dB rear vs. 109dB).INSTALLATIONInstallation took me about 10 minutes. It would've been even quicker if I didn't have to move one of my other cards out of the way to install it. My PCI-E x1 slot was taken up by my USB 3.0 expansion card so I inserted it into my other PCI-E slot. Also, unlike other sound cards I've used in the past, the Xonar DX required it's own power so I had to use the included Molex adapter and plug it into my power supply. I disabled my onboard audio in the BIOS, installed the latest Windows 7 64-bit drivers, rebooted and was in business.SOUND QUALITYI began my audio testing by playing my FLAC audio files on my puny built-in speakers on my Samsung monitor. All of the sudden, the sound quality was actually bearable coming from my monitor. The clarity of the audio improved by a factor of two or three. I then moved onto my headphones-- my primary reason for upgrading. I plugged my Sennheiser HD 555's into my front panel headphone jack but got no sound. Oops, did I install the header pins backwards? I opened my case back up and double checked but all looked well. I then realized that the driver installation also installed the Xonar DX Audio Center application and I had to manually switch the analog out to the front panel headphone jack. Eww. The Realtek onboard audio chip automatically detected when I inserted headphones in and swapped the audio over to them without my intervention. This would have been a hassle not worth dealing with had the sound quality pumping through my headphones not been amazing.My music sounded wonderful! The bass was immensely improved on my bass-challenged HD 555's and every other measure of sound quality was noticeably improved over the onboard audio I'd been used to listening to for three years. Next up were movies. I played high action scenes from the last Star Trek movie and Avatar and was, B-L-O-W-N away. I fiddled with the Dolby Headphone settings and realized for the first time that they weren't gimmicks at all. I truly felt surrounded by the motion picture. I love action adventure and science fiction films and I now had a proper setup for optimum enjoyment! Also, the noisy audio from my PC was virtually eliminated. With the onboard audio, I heard all the EMF interference but with the Asus Xonar DX, it was barely audible.GAMESI was a big-time gamer back when Half-Life, Unreal Tournament and WarCraft III were out. These days, fatherhood has had a serious impact on my ability to find time for games so aside from the occasional game of Bejeweled, I only find myself playing Age of Empires III. I thought the sound was terrific but I can't judge just how great it works with more modern games. I do know that due to the software-based support of EAX 5.0, games that use EAX aren't quite as good as having hardware support of EAX 5.0, like the X-Fi Titanium.CONCLUSIONI am over the moon with the Asus Xonar DX. Music and movies have never sounded so good on my PC. If you have EAX 5.0 games, you might be better off with the X-Fi Titanium, but I really needed support for front-panel headers. Maybe some day I will be able to justify the audiophile quality audio cards, but until then, I will be enjoying the Xonar DX without regret. I can't recommend this card highly enough.

review_text: Review for MDR-IF240RK... Have had these headphones for about 2 months now, and they work really well for one of the most common and basic wireless headphone uses - listening to TV.  My need arises from the fact that other members of family practice musical instruments (usually by listening to instruments with headphones on) in the same room as our primary audio-visual system, so I too needed a headphone solution to avoid conflicting with the silent music practice.  Here are the deets:- battery life is fine... even when listening for hours I've never lost juice- have even fallen asleep with phones on and they still had charge in the am, and yes they are comfortable enough to doze off...- you do have to be a bit precise when putting the headphones back in the charger/base station cradle, as the charging prongs need to line up with metal contacts on the headphones... not a big deal but the headphones don't always make electrical contact if you casually pop them into the cradle- headphones are surprisingly lightweight, a bit heavier than but in the same class as, say, old school open air Sennheisers... even though the battery (left side) and volume control/electronics (right side) are on the headset... they are also evenly weighted left/right, probably because the aaa battery weighs similar to electronics- REALLY like use of standard rechargeable AAA battery... no need to dump $$$ into proprietary batteries- I find the foam ear pads slightly warm, but no different than typical open air headphones, and definitely not at sweatbox level that can be the case with closed headphones- adjustment of earpiece height is, so far, very workable... The earpieces simply pull down out if the headband... they are lightly spring loaded, so retract when you take them off your head, but they stay adjusted to the height you pull them down to because there is a slight friction feed which holds them in place when the headband is splayed open to put them on your head... this sounds complex but it's really natural and well engineered (only issue would be if the spring weakens over the course of long-term use, but no sign of that yet)- volume level, which you adjust on the right earpiece, is more than adequate for TV shows, fidelity is also fine for TV but certainly not up to task of serious listening to music... amazingly, range and tone is pretty good for movies... BluRay disc quality 'lows and highs' in movies like Avatar come through quite well- I find it easy to adjust volume while wearing headphones...GREAT for muting out the commercials without grabbing the remote- being open design, you can hear people talking in the same room, so don't buy these if you're trying to tune out a lot of ambient noise - on the other hand if you DO need to hear things in the room or area of the house (e.g. baby monitoring) these headphones can be worn very comfortably with one earpiece pushed forward or backward- regarding range... don't buy IR headphones for extreme range... these have easily 50 foot plus range but the real consideration is that they only work within view of the base station... this is pretty tolerant - even if you can't literally see the base station they work, so not as twitchy as I feared and it can actually be a good feature, as when you walk out of the room to talk with someone, the sound mutes cleanly and completely, so no need to take them off and no worries about partial or intermittent sound- IMPT: ZERO interference from WiFi or wireless phones... a big deal because I sit within 6 feet of our wireless router... Infrared is the key here and IR zero interference is main reason why I went only for IR

review_title: Good router; many features, compact footprint, decent user interface...
review_text: The Netgear N300 (JNR3210) is a solidly performing router with more features than you might expect for this price (this is especially so with a rebate available for purchases by March 31, 2013).This router performs basic wired and wireless Internet access functions very well. Set-up was relatively easy. Using a wired port for the initial set-up, it immediately recognized my provider's connection. After entering the default user name/password (via its internal web server) it provided a prompt that a firmware update was available. I was given the option to accept the update or not. I did, and in less than five minutes was working with the router again. I performed all other configuration options via a wireless adapter.Pros:-Wired connection/activity LEDs on front panel.-Pushbutton wireless on/off button on front panel.-Home and guest network (and options to integrate or separate them).-Separately configurable SSID and security settings for the home and guest networks.-Usable as both a gateway (connected to the provider) and as an access point (connected to another router's wired port)-Multiple security options-Options to reserve bandwidth (50% to 80%) for trusted internal IP addresses (for streaming and gaming performance).-Parental controls. Basic controls include setting up on/off times for wireless operation; additional controls require a Netgear program download (that I did not test).-Hardware access control: MAC address filtering.-Multiple security protocol options.-Compact footprint; significantly smaller than many other similarly performing routers.Also available is a USB connection usable for sharing printer or data devices (because I'm already using DLNA via a separate NAS, I did not test this feature).The user interface is generally intuitive and will be familiar to users of other Netgear products. The router offers options for either guided setup (through its "Genie" interface) or manual input of both basic and advanced functions.Cons (all minor, but worth being prepared for)-No install CD. While this did not hinder the router's installation, it requires you navigate Netgear's support site to download the user guide...which most users WILL want to do. It's detailed, complete and 122 pages long.-External antennas. Not an issue for me, but some may not like this look.Overall, this router provides "basic and then some" features at a "basic" price.
